newsitem.title: UK: Banks plan disposal of William Hill chain - paper.
newsitem.headline: Banks plan disposal of William Hill chain - paper.

text.p: Banks in control of debt-laden British leisure company Brent Walker Broup Plc have drawn up plans to realise the value of the company's William Hill betting shop chain, the Times reported on Monday.
The paper said Close Brothers, Brent Walker's merchant bank, had been asked to review a number of options for the profitable 1,700-strong William Hill chain.
These included a straight sale, a stock market flotation or a reversal of the chain into the old Brent Walker shell.
Analysts said William Hill, bought by Brent Walker in 1989, would be valued at between 500 million pounds ($817.1 million) and 600 million pounds ($980.5 million).
Brent Walker sold its Pubmaster pub chain to Berryboss for 171.3 million pounds ($279.9 million) in November.
